description: The journal's cap on a declared context field's value (spec/journal.md, "Declared context fields"): at most maxBytes bytes of UTF-8 canonical JSON (object keys sorted, no whitespace, numbers as JavaScript writes them) is kept in `context`, and a larger value's name goes in `contextOmitted`. `json` is the value as received; `bytes` is the length of its canonical JSON. Expected values from the TypeScript reference. Regenerate with node spec/vectors/generate-journal-context-cap.mjs.

cases.description: an ASCII string at the cap
an ASCII string a byte under the cap
an ASCII string a byte over the cap
an object received with whitespace and unsorted keys, at the cap once canonical: the received text is longer
whole numbers received as 1.0, at the cap: JavaScript writes 1, 2.5, -3, 0 and 100
exponents, a byte over the cap: JavaScript writes 1e+21 and 2e+22
large and small magnitudes, a byte over the cap: JavaScript writes 100000000000000000000, 0.000001 and 0.0000015 in full
shortest round-trip decimals at the cap: 0.1 is 0.1, and 1e-7 and beyond take an exponent
negative zero at the cap: JavaScript writes 0
integers past 2^53, a byte over the cap: JavaScript writes the double it reads, so 99999999999999999 is 100000000000000000
three-byte characters a byte over the cap, though far under 4096 characters or UTF-16 code units
four-byte characters (UTF-16 surrogate pairs) at the cap
escapes in the received text count as the characters they encode, at the cap: \u00e9, \u20ac, a surrogate pair and \/
quotes, backslashes and the short escapes take two bytes each, a byte over the cap
other control characters take six bytes each, a byte over the cap
DEL, U+2028 and U+2029 are written as they are, at the cap
escapes and multibyte characters in object keys count too, a byte over the cap
nested objects and arrays with keys out of order, a byte under the cap
